title: A Prom for the Detention
premise: Elodie Zhou, a debate champion whose home life is a losing argument, has perfected the art of invisibility at Marrow Creek High — until notes signed by the school's legendary ghost, Wren Halloway (a student who vanished in 1987), begin appearing in their locker, written in ink that shouldn't exist. As Elodie investigates with their only friend, Priya, the ghost's messages force them to confront what really happened the night of the infamous 1987 prom and why Elodie's own family has spent decades avoiding the school. The truth: Wren never died; she ran away after being outed at prom, and she is Elodie's great-aunt, alive but dying, leaving notes through her old friend, the school custodian. In the end, Elode must choose between protecting their family's silence and telling the truth publicly — a speech at senior prom that costs them Priya's trust temporarily but wins it back forever, as Wren returns to see the dance she never got.
about_author: Sebastian Whitlock is the pen name of a former high-school debate coach who spent seven years listening to teenagers argue their way past truths they couldn't say aloud. They write from a small coastal town where every old building allegedly has a ghost, and most of them do.

chapters.title: Ninety-Three Days
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Opening on a debate tournament win that means nothing at home, Elodie counts down to graduation and establishes their survival strategy: perfect grades, zero attention. Emotional beat: weary resignation disguised as ambition.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Never Left
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. During detention for a fight they didn't start, the custodian Mr. Okafor tells the legend of Wren Halloway, who vanished before the 1987 prom. Elodie feels an odd pull they can't name. Beat: uneasy curiosity breaking through numbness.

chapters.title: Ink That Isn't Ink
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A note appears in their locker: 'You argue beautifully, Elodie Zhou. But do you ever say anything true?' The handwriting shimmers like wet ink that never dries. Beat: fear mixed with the thrill of being seen.

chapters.title: Priya Doesn't Believe in Ghosts
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Skeptical Priya insists it's a prank, but agrees to help investigate to protect Elodie. Their friendship dynamics emerge — Priya protective, Elodie evasive even with her. Beat: loyalty tested by secrets.

chapters.title: The Yearbook Gap
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. In the archive, they discover Wren's photo has been cut from every 1987 yearbook — deliberately. Someone wanted her erased. At home, Elodie notices the same face in a hidden family photo album. Beat: dawning dread.

chapters.title: Mother Knows the Name
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Confronting their mother triggers a shutdown: 'Some things stay buried.' Elodie realizes the family silence and the school silence are the same silence. Beat: the first real crack in the wall between Elodie and home.

chapters.title: Notes in Impossible Places
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Notes escalate — inside Elodie's debate folder mid-tournament, on the bathroom mirror. Priya watches Elodie unravel and fears the notes are self-harm in disguise. Beat: love expressed as worry, misread as accusation.

chapters.title: Mr. Okafor's Keys
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie catches Mr. Okafor near their locker at midnight and confronts him. He admits delivering the notes but not writing them — he receives them too, and has for thirty-seven years. Beat: vertigo; the impossible becomes structural.

chapters.title: What Happened Before the Dance
chapters.summary: Dual investigation, Elodie's POV. Reconstructing 1987 through microfilm: Wren was outed at prom, humiliated, and disappeared that night. Everyone assumed the worst. Elodie recognizes the cruelty as timeless — the same kids' logic runs the halls now. Beat: righteous anger.

chapters.title: The Argument Elodie Can't Win
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A family dinner detonates when Elodie says Wren's name aloud. Their mother leaves the table; their grandmother weeps. Elodie learns Wren was their grandmother's sister. Beat: grief finally given a shape and a name.

chapters.title: She's Alive
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Mr. Okafor reveals the truth: Wren ran, built a life two states away, and is now dying. She wanted to reach one descendant brave enough to finish her sentence. Priya urges Elodie to go meet her. Beat: hope arriving terrifyingly late.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Miles of Silence
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Road trip with Priya to meet Wren. In the car, Elodie confesses everything they've hidden about home; Priya admits she's been scared of losing Elodie to the ghost story. Beat: intimacy forged in motion.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Meeting Wren: sharp, funny, unrepentant, oxygen tank beside her armchair. She doesn't want pity or apology — she wants to know if the school still eats its invisible kids. Elodie can't honestly say it doesn't. Beat: devastating clarity.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.summary: Wren's request via letter, Elodie's POV: tell the truth at senior prom, publicly, where she was destroyed. Elodie refuses — it would cost everything. Wren: 'It already cost me everything. Silence just charges interest.' Beat: refusal and resentment.

chapters.title: Detention, Again
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Back at school, Elodie goes cold and robotic, throwing themselves into debate finals. Priya sees the cost of carrying Wren's secret alone and demands Elodie stop shutting her out. Fight. Beat: friendship fracture.

chapters.title: The Final Round
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. State debate final: assigned to argue a position they don't believe. Mid-speech, Elodie freezes — then abandons the case and tells the judges a true story instead. They lose. It's the first honest thing they've done all year. Beat: liberating defeat.

chapters.title: Prom Tickets
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Prom approaches; Priya buys two tickets on impulse, unsure if they're speaking. Elodie finds them and asks, 'Will you be there when I say it?' Priya: 'I'll be there whether I forgive you yet or not.' Beat: tentative repair.

chapters.title: The Night Of
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Gym transformed, same banners as 1987. Elodie takes the microphone during the slow song and tells Wren's story — and their own — to a stunned gymnasium. Some students laugh; some cry; one teacher quietly turns off the music, then turns it back on. Beat: terror transfigured into courage.

chapters.title: The Cost
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs across the aftermath week. Fallout: viral video, furious administration, a grandmother who won't speak to Elodie — but also students coming forward with their own buried stories. Priya stands beside Elodie in the principal's office. Beat: consequences and unexpected solidarity.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Door
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie visits their grandmother, who finally opens the box of Wren's letters she's kept for decades. Through tears she admits she chose silence to survive and let her sister carry the exile alone. Beat: generational grief met with forgiveness.

chapters.title: A Prom for Wren
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The senior class votes to hold a second, unofficial dance in the gym — everyone invited, no one erased. Wren arrives in a wheelchair, wearing the dress she never got to wear, and dances one slow song with Elodie. Beat: belonging, hard-won and imperfect.

chapters.title: Day One
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, graduation morning. Wren has died peacefully; her final note reads simply, 'Thank you for saying it out loud.' Elodie crosses the stage, no longer counting days but starting them, Priya's hand in theirs. Beat: quiet, earned hope — survival traded for a life.
